package.name: twilio
package.packageFile:
# TWILIO — the carrier, so a voice node can be on a real phone call instead of in a browser.
#
# ONE NODE, and it is an ATTACHMENT rather than a box you wire in (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §14).
# That is the whole design decision in this package, and it is worth reading before adding to it.
#
# A phone call cannot travel on a data edge in either direction. A voice node's run IS the call,
# held open for its whole length, and its outputs fire at the end: a phone node downstream of it
# would run after the call was over, and one upstream would have to complete while still holding
# the socket. Nor is it a service, because a service is something the host CALLS and gets one
# value back from.
#
# So the phone is not part of any voice node. It is the LANE the run is speaking on, and it
# arrives as configuration that clips on and locks what it owns. One attachment, and every voice
# node rides it unchanged — Realtime, GPT-Live, Grok Voice — because none of them contains a
# phone. See docs/VOICE_STREAMING_GUIDE.md "The Phone Lane".
#
# MEDIA STREAMS, NOT CONVERSATIONRELAY. ConversationRelay does speech-to-text and text-to-speech
# for you and hands back text, which would mean paying for a realtime voice model and never using
# its voice. Media Streams gives raw call audio both ways, which is what a voice model wants.

name: twilio
displayName: Twilio
description: Real phone numbers for voice nodes, and WhatsApp messaging
version: 1.0.0
category: communication
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1789899519/gravity/icons/twillio-logo.png

features:
  - A voice node on a real phone number, over Media Streams

allowedHosts:
  - api.twilio.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"

credentials.twilioCredential.yaml:
# ONE credential for the whole account: the phone line today, WhatsApp when it lands.
#
# The Auth Token is the account's master secret. An API Key SID/Secret pair is the better
# practice (it can be revoked without rotating everything), but the account SID plus auth token
# is what Twilio's own console shows first and what every tutorial uses, so it is what someone
# setting this up for the first time will have in front of them.
name: twilioCredential
displayName: Twilio
description: Twilio account credentials for voice and messaging

properties:
  - name: accountSid
    displayName: Account SID
    type: string
    required: true
    # NOT a secret, and saying so explicitly. The SID identifies the account and appears in
    # every request URL; the auth token beside it is the thing worth hiding.
    secret: false
    description: Your Account SID, on the Twilio console home page. Starts with AC
    placeholder: AC00000000000000000000000000000000

  - name: authToken
    displayName: Auth Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Auth Token, beside the Account SID on the console home page
    placeholder: Enter your Twilio auth token

files.config.yaml:
# THIS ATTACHMENT'S OWN SETTINGS. They are not the host's: they reach the run under
# `attachments.TwilioLine`, so a field of the same name on a voice node stays that node's own.
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [direction]
  properties:
    direction:
      type: string
      title: Direction
      description: >-
        Whether the workflow places the call, or waits for one. Outbound calls the number below
        when the voice node runs. Inbound answers whoever rings your Twilio number.
      enum: [outbound, inbound]
      enumNames: [Outbound, Inbound]
      default: outbound

    to:
      type: string
      title: Number to call
      description: >-
        In E.164 form, so +447700900123 rather than 07700 900123. Outbound only. Shared blocks
        and upstream data work here, which is how a workflow calls a different person each run.
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies":
        direction: outbound

    from:
      type: string
      title: Caller ID
      description: >-
        Which of your Twilio numbers the call comes from, in E.164 form. Inbound, this is the
        number being answered.
      "ui:field": template

    # VOICEMAIL IS THE CASE THAT WILL BITE, so it is a setting rather than something the model
    # is left to work out. A single-minded call that leaves a coherent message is a different
    # script from one that holds a conversation, and from inside the call the two sound alike.
    onVoicemail:
      type: string
      title: If voicemail answers
      description: >-
        Hanging up keeps the call log honest, so the workflow can try again later. Leaving a
        message speaks the opening line once and then ends the call.
      enum: [hangUp, leaveMessage]
      enumNames: [Hang up, Leave the opening line as a message]
      default: hangUp
      "ui:dependencies":
        direction: outbound

    ringSeconds:
      type: number
      title: Ring for
      description: How many seconds to let it ring before giving up. Outbound only.
      default: 30
      minimum: 5
      maximum: 120
      "ui:dependencies":
        direction: outbound

"ui:order": [direction, to, from, onVoicemail, ringSeconds]
files.interface.yaml:
# WHAT CLIPPING THIS ON DOES (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §14).
#
# No inputs, no outputs, no serviceConnectors, and no api/ folder at all. This node never runs.
attaches:
  # ONE FIELD, and that is deliberate. An earlier draft also set the sample rate and the codec
  # here, which was wrong in a way worth recording: those are not choices, they are facts of the
  # lane. Twilio is G.711 mu-law at 8 kHz because the phone network is, and the runtime knows
  # that the moment it knows the lane. Putting them in config would be offering a decision that
  # has exactly one correct answer, and a wrong sample rate is not an error anywhere — the model
  # simply transcribes at the wrong speed and it reads as poor accuracy.
  sets:
    lane: twilio

  # CONTRIBUTED TO THE HOST'S RUN, so the voice node runs holding two credentials: its own
  # vendor key, and this one. Neither node writes into the other, and the picker for this one
  # appears on the tab this attachment adds to the voice node's panel.
  credentials:
    - name: twilioCredential
      required: true
      displayName: Twilio

  # WHAT THE HOST BECOMES while this is clipped on.
  #
  # A voice node in a browser emits nothing outside the platform and rightly declares nothing.
  # The very same node with this clipped on DIALS A REAL HUMAN BEING, and a build loop re-runs a
  # workflow after every stage — so without this, each attempt would ring a real telephone. A
  # placed call has no inverse, so a test run traces it instead.
  capabilities:
    emitsExternally: true
files.node.yaml:
type: TwilioLine
kind: Attachment

name: Twilio Phone Line
# On the canvas it is a sill under a node, beside its own logo, so the vendor is all it has to
# say. The full name is for the picker, where it sits among a hundred others.
displayName: Twilio
category: Voice
color: "#F22F46"

description: Puts a voice node on a real phone call instead of in the browser

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when the conversation should happen on a real phone number rather than in a browser tab,
  either because the workflow is calling someone or because someone is calling in. Clips onto a
  voice node and changes nothing about it: the model, the voice, the prompt and the tools all
  stay exactly as they are, because only the lane the audio travels on is different.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS. An attachment never runs, so it adds no requirement of its own and there is
# nothing here for a requirement to narrow. The node it is clipped to owns that question.
auth:
  required: false
